# Implementation Plan: Fix the crews hook-timeout cascade (lock-contention + hot-lock starvation)
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"crews-hook-timeout-under-lock-contention"} -->


*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-10. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-hook-timeout-under-lock-contention/plan.md`.*

Target repo: the **`ai-developer-toolkit` submodule**, package `plugins/crews/` (crews **v3.19.1**).
Impl is a **lead-owned two-commit submodule flow** (submodule commit + push, then codexu pointer bump). This plan
describes that ceremony but the impl member does NOT push to the submodule's `main` or bump the codexu pointer.

## Overview

crews PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop hooks frequently die at the engine's hard hook timeout (5s for Pre/Post,
10s for Stop on codex AND Claude; Copilot declares 30s and is ~immune). The operator-confirmed framing is that
**raising the timeout is a band-aid** — the timeouts trip *far too often* because of a self-sustaining design
defect, not an occasional slow disk. The investigation
(`.ralph/investigations/crews-hook-timeout-under-lock-contention/findings.md`) confirmed the mechanism in three
layers: (1) an **orphan-lock cascade** — a hook killed for blowing its deadline leaves a `.lock` that is
non-stealable for 30s, so one slow write detonates a 30s storm where every following hook on that manifest also
times out and leaves its own orphan lock; (2) a **hot-lock design** — a single per-actor `manifest.json` lock
serializes the ~10s heartbeat timer, every per-tool-call hook, and (for leads) mailbox ops, so one slow write
starves everything behind it, *including the heartbeat* (which is why the lead listener keeps getting reaped);
and (3) **per-hook I/O + syscall volume** — every tool call spawns two fresh node hook processes that each
read+atomically-rewrite the manifest, the Stop hook reads the full `events.jsonl`, and lock files churn per
fire, a flood of file ops that itself invites the Windows-Defender real-time-scan locks that trigger the slow
writes in the first place (via the intentional ~6.5s AV-resilience retry budget in `hooks/safe-io.js`).

This plan **centers the real fix (L3)** — kill the cascade, de-contend the hot lock, and cut per-hook I/O —
and folds the timeout bump (L2) and Defender-exclusion docs (L1) in as *mitigations that must not substitute
for L3*. The AV-resilience budget on the listener-heartbeat path is preserved in full; only idempotent/advisory
hook manifest writes get a tighter fail-open budget, protocol-state writes stay fail-loud, and the heartbeat is
moved off the contended manifest lock entirely.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context
All four research lenses (researcher, architect, codex, copilot) converge on the same map and design; the
consolidated brief is in `research-brief.md`. Confirmed sites:
- `hooks/locks.js`: `LOCK_STALE_MS = 30000` (`:20`); `writeNewLockFile()` ALREADY persists `{ pid, owner, acquiredAt, hostname }` (`:41-60`); `lockIsStealable()` uses only acquiredAt/mtime, **no PID liveness today** (`:71-90`); `acquireLock()` EEXIST/steal loop (`:134-155`); `withManifestLock`/`withMailboxLock` default 2000ms (`:186-224`).
- `hooks/safe-io.js`: retry budget 10×exp-backoff = ~6500ms cumulative (`:41-65`); `renameSyncWithRetry` is synchronous with an injectable `sleepFn` seam + `onRetrySuccess` (`:125-155`); `writeJsonAtomicWithRetry` unique-temp+rename (`:157-175`).
- `hooks/actors.js`: `writeManifest`→`writeJsonAtomic` (`:618-628`), `updateManifest` read-merge-rewrite (`:631-638`); `touchHeartbeat` + `markArmIntent` rewrite the FULL manifest UNDER `withManifestLock` (`:1073-1177`); `FRESH_ARM_GUARD_STATES = {armed, exited, never-armed}`.
- `hooks/health.js`: `isProcessAlive(pid)` = `process.kill(pid,0)` (ESRCH→false, EPERM→true, true|false|null) (`:13-23`).
- `hooks/actor-state.js::deriveListenerState`: `HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS_LOCAL = 5*60_000`; stale `lastHeartbeatAt` → `exited`; `isStaleArmedManifest` also checks `isProcessAlive(lastListenerPid)===false` (`:54-96`).
- `lib/listener-loop.js`: heartbeat timer calls `markArmed({sessionId,listenerPid})` each tick (`:358-407`).
- Per-hook writes are mostly ALREADY conditional: `pre-tool-use.js` writes only `markArmIntent` on arm-calls; `post-tool-use.js` writes only `claimNagSeq` when a nag is due. The UNCONDITIONAL recurring writes are the heartbeat tick and `turn-observability.js` (`updateManifest` on every new transcript message, `:258-277`).
- Full `events.jsonl` reads each fire: `detect-active-bg.js::readEvents` (`:126-144`) and `turn-observability.js::extractLatestAssistantMessage` (`:114-153`).
- Timeouts: `.codex-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` + `hooks/hooks.json` = 5/5/10 (Pre/Post/Stop); `.github/plugin/hooks.json` = 30s.
- Release: crews **3.19.1**; `scripts/bump-version.js` edits 6 files; `tests/version.test.js` pins; `hooks/config.js` re-export surface pinned by `tests/split-export-compat.test.js` (exact count).

### Technical Constraints
- **AV-resilience must be preserved on the heartbeat path.** The ~6.5s `safe-io` budget exists (v3.5.0/3.8.0) to survive Defender real-time-scan locks on long-lived heartbeats. Do NOT globally shrink it. Only idempotent/advisory hook manifest writes get a tighter, fail-open budget.
- **No `locks.js → health.js` import (cycle).** `health.js` imports `actors.js`, and `actors.js`/`config.js` already depend on `locks.js`. The dead-PID liveness check must come from a LEAF module (or a local conservative helper), not `require('./health')`.
- **L3b must not lose concurrent manifest updates or protocol state.** The manifest lock currently serializes a read-modify-write. Naively releasing the lock before the rename can clobber a newer manifest. The chosen design (single attempt under lock + fail-open, retry-next-hook) is allowed ONLY for idempotent/advisory writes such as `markArmIntent`, `claimNagSeq`, and `turn-observability`. Protocol-state writes — `consumeMailbox` cursor/review-required/operator-direct updates, outbox/report finalization, and the final Stop `lastSeq`/review gate manifest update — stay fail-loud/transactional. In particular, `consumeMailbox` must not empty `mailbox.json` unless the matching manifest cursor patch can commit.
- **L3c must preserve v3.6.2 listener-epoch ownership + the `requireFreshArm` duplicate-listener guard + `recoverable` takeover fencing.** Initial arm still claims epoch/PID under the manifest lock; only recurring heartbeat ticks move to the stamp.
- **`config.js` export-count is snapshot-pinned.** Any new export added there bumps `tests/split-export-compat.test.js`. Prefer leaf-module-only exports for new helpers (the v3.12.0 precedent).
- **Windows test runner.** `node tests/run.js` is worker-per-file with per-worker temp HOME/CREWS_HOME; race-sensitive lock/listener tests go in the `DEFAULT_SERIAL_DENYLIST` (`tests/run.js:39`). Git Bash must be first on PATH for the bash-stub tests.

## Approach

### Architecture
A single, internally-consistent fix that attacks the cascade at its root rather than widening the deadline:

1. **Break the cascade at the lock (L3a).** Reclaim an orphaned lock the instant its holder process is proven
   dead, instead of waiting the 30s staleness window. Because a codex-killed hook's `.lock` carries the dead
   hook's PID, the very next waiter reclaims it immediately — the storm cannot sustain.
2. **Stop pinning the lock across advisory slow writes (L3b).** Idempotent/advisory hook-context manifest writes
   do a single atomic-write attempt under the lock and fail open on a transient AV lock (logging cheaply,
   retrying on the next hook fire). Protocol-state writes stay fail-loud/transactional; their cascade relief
   comes from L3a immediate steal and L3c heartbeat de-contention, not from fail-open.
3. **Take the heartbeat off the hot lock (L3c).** Recurring heartbeat ticks write a tiny lock-free per-actor
   stamp file; the path-aware `getListenerState(name, crew, stateCwd, opts)` wrapper reads it and feeds that
   freshness into the derived listener-state result ONLY when the stamp still belongs to the manifest's current
   listener owner (`stamp.pid === manifest.lastListenerPid` AND `stamp.epoch === manifest.lastListenerEpoch`).
   Ignore orphan/superseded stamps and fall back to `manifest.lastHeartbeatAt`/stale handling. Keep
   `deriveListenerState(manifest)` manifest-only/pure, with `manifest.lastHeartbeatAt` as the back-compat
   fallback. A slow hook holding the manifest lock can no longer starve the current listener's heartbeat → the
   lead-listener reap (the hot-lock variety) stops.
4. **Cut per-hook I/O (L3d).** Coalesce no-op manifest writes (the heartbeat move already removes the biggest
   recurring write) and replace the two full-`events.jsonl` reads with a shared bounded tail reader.
5. **Mitigations (do not substitute for L3).** L2: raise codex/Claude Pre/Post/Stop timeouts to 30s. L1:
   document `.crews/` Defender exclusions.

### Implementation Strategy (ordered)
Before threading the L3b fail-open helper, classify every manifest-write call site it may touch and keep the
helper mechanically limited to the approved advisory rows:

| Safety class | Manifest-write call sites | Required behavior |
|---|---|---|
| BEST-EFFORT / advisory hook context | `turn-observability.js` `updateManifest` for `lastObservedAssistantMessageId`/turn-observability fields; `post-tool-use.js::claimNagSeq` writing `lastMidTurnNagSeq`; `pre-tool-use.js` `markArmIntent` writing arm intent | May use the single-attempt fail-open helper; log `hook-write-budget-exhausted`; rely on the next hook fire to retry. |
| MUST-COMMIT / transactional protocol state | `mailbox.js::consumeMailbox` drain/cursor/review-required/operator-direct patch; Stop outbox/report finalization and empty-body retry manifest updates; final Stop `lastSeq`/`lastTurnAt`/review-gate update after durable outbox append; `touchHeartbeat`'s initial v3.6.2 listener epoch/PID arm claim | Never use the fail-open helper; keep the full transactional path fail-loud/blocking so state is not partially committed or silently corrupted. |

1. **L3a — dead-holder lock-steal.** Add a leaf liveness helper (`hooks/process-liveness.js`, exporting `isProcessAlive(pid)` returning `true|false|null`; have `hooks/health.js` re-export from it so there is one implementation). In `acquireLock`, on `EEXIST`, read the lock; if `hostname === os.hostname()` AND the PID is a sane positive int AND `isProcessAlive(pid) === false` AND `acquiredAt`/mtime are not implausibly in the future, steal immediately via the existing `.steal` mutex path. Otherwise fall through to the existing `lockIsStealable` 30s path. Add an injectable liveness seam (option arg / module-level override) so tests don't depend on real PIDs. Apply the SAME host-scoped dead-PID immediate-steal to the `.steal` mutex acquisition (`acquireStealMutex`, `hooks/locks.js:92-119`), which today also waits only the 30s mtime staleness: a hook killed while holding `<lock>.steal` must not reintroduce a 30s stall in front of the main lock's immediate dead-PID recovery.
2. **L3b — hook-context write budget.** First classify every `mailbox.js`/`actors.js` manifest-write caller as advisory, heartbeat, or protocol before adding any budget plumbing. Then add a `budgetKind: 'advisory-hook' | 'heartbeat' | 'protocol'` (or `maxAttempts`/`deadlineMs` plus an explicit `failOpen` flag) option to `writeJsonAtomicWithRetry`/`renameSyncWithRetry` in `safe-io.js`, keeping the fail-open helper mechanically opt-in only at the approved idempotent/advisory hook call sites (`markArmIntent`, `claimNagSeq`, `turn-observability`) rather than exposing it as a generalized `mailbox.js` write mode. Advisory hook context = one atomic-write attempt under the manifest lock; on transient exhaustion, FAIL-OPEN (return a sentinel / log `hook-write-budget-exhausted`) and let the next hook retry. Protocol-state writes stay FAIL-LOUD / transactional: `consumeMailbox`'s inbox-history + mailbox-clear + `lastInboxSeq`/`lastReviewRequiredSeq`/operator-direct cursor update must abort without emptying `mailbox.json` if the cursor patch cannot commit; outbox/report finalization and the final Stop `lastSeq`/review-required manifest update must also throw/block rather than fail open. Heartbeat/listener calls keep the default full budget.
3. **L3c — lock-free heartbeat stamp.** `touchHeartbeat`/the listener timer writes `<actorDir>/heartbeat` (a tiny `{ ts, pid, epoch }` JSON using the listener's captured PID and granted epoch) WITHOUT the manifest lock, keeping the full AV retry budget on that small write. Do NOT make `deriveListenerState(manifest)` read the stamp: it is intentionally pure and has manifest-only call sites. Instead, teach `getListenerState(name, crew, stateCwd, opts)` and a shared stamp-aware heartbeat freshness helper to resolve the actor dir, read the stamp, and use `stamp.ts` as the primary freshness signal ONLY when `stamp.pid` and `stamp.epoch` match the current manifest's `lastListenerPid` and `lastListenerEpoch`; if either ownership token differs, ignore the stamp as orphan/superseded and fall back to `manifest.lastHeartbeatAt` (or stale handling) exactly as if the stamp were absent. Update path-aware gates and status/list surfaces that currently call `deriveListenerState(current)` or compute heartbeat age from `manifest.lastHeartbeatAt` directly — at minimum `writeLeadTakeoverManifest`/`writeMemberTakeoverManifest`, `touchHeartbeat`, `mailbox.js::isQueuedWhileUnarmed`, `health.js::getMemberHealth`, and `crews.js::snapshotCrew`/`list-members` liveness rows — to use the stamp-aware path when `name`/`crew`/`cwd` are available, or document why any remaining manifest-only consumer is safe on the manifest fallback. The INITIAL arm still writes `lastListenerEpoch`/`lastListenerPid`/`listenerState` under the manifest lock; recurring ticks no longer rewrite the full manifest. Preserve `requireFreshArm`/`FRESH_ARM_GUARD_STATES` and the `recoverable` fence.
4. **L3d — reduce per-hook I/O.** (a) In `updateManifest`, skip the write when the merged result equals the current manifest (no-op coalescing). (b) Extract a shared bounded `readEventsTail(path, maxBytes/maxLines)` helper and use it in both `detect-active-bg.js` and `turn-observability.js` instead of full `readFileSync`. (c) Add a TESTS-ONLY fs-op counter in the regression test (monkeypatch or injected fs object inside the test only; do not plumb counters through production hook APIs) to assert the concrete Copilot `PostToolUse` turn-observability fixture in the AC below drops below its measured pre-fix operation count.
5. **L2 — timeout bump.** Set Pre/Post/Stop to 30s in `.codex-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` and `hooks/hooks.json`. Leave `.github/plugin/hooks.json` (Copilot) at 30s.
6. **L1 — Defender-exclusion docs.** Add a short ops note to the plugin-local `plugins/crews/AGENTS.md` (MANDATORY) describing adding the `.crews/` state dirs to Windows Defender real-time-scan exclusions; also add it to `README.md` only if operator-facing setup already lives there.
7. **Release plumbing (impl member runs; lead owns the push).** `node scripts/bump-version.js <next>` (minor bump, e.g. 3.20.0), prepend a `CHANGELOG.md` entry, add the `## vX.Y.Z` section to `plugins/crews/AGENTS.md`. Run `node tests/version.test.js`. Do NOT push the submodule `main` or bump the codexu pointer — that is the lead-owned two-commit ceremony.

- **Watch:** `hooks/config.js` re-export surface (`tests/split-export-compat.test.js` exact-count) — prefer leaf-only exports for new helpers.

## Scope

### In Scope
- L3a dead-holder host-scoped immediate lock-steal + leaf liveness helper.
- L3b advisory hook-context single-attempt-fail-open manifest write budget (heartbeat keeps full AV budget; protocol-state writes stay fail-loud/transactional).
- L3c lock-free per-actor heartbeat stamp consumed by path-aware `getListenerState(...)` (+ back-compat manifest fallback while keeping `deriveListenerState(manifest)` pure).
- L3d no-op manifest-write coalescing + shared bounded `events.jsonl` tail reader + file-op-count test.
- L2 codex/Claude Pre/Post/Stop timeout → 30s.
- L1 Defender-exclusion ops docs.
- Version bump + CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md section + marketplace sync (impl member); the required tests.

### Out of Scope
- The attached-async-shell idle-reap mechanism (separate task `crews-listener-silent-reap-across-idle-investigation` — different root; see Bundle decision).
- Any global reduction of the `safe-io` AV-resilience retry budget.
- A daemon/database replacement for `.crews/` file state (explicitly anti-recommended in crews AGENTS.md).
- The lead-owned submodule push + codexu pointer bump + `copilot plugin update` ceremony (described, not executed).
- macOS/Linux-specific lock behavior beyond keeping the existing cross-platform `isProcessAlive` semantics intact.

## Risk Areas
- **Circular import** if liveness is pulled from `health.js` into `locks.js`. Mitigation: leaf module `process-liveness.js`; `health.js` re-exports it.
- **PID reuse** stealing a *fresh* lock whose PID was recycled onto an unrelated live/dead process. Mitigation: host-scope (`hostname` match) + pair the dead-PID check with the existing `acquiredAt`/future-time sanity; only steal when BOTH dead-PID and not-implausibly-fresh.
- **Orphaned `.steal` mutex** reintroducing the 30s stall even after L3a's main-lock dead-PID steal. Mitigation: `acquireStealMutex` (`hooks/locks.js:92-119`) gets the same host-scoped dead-PID immediate-steal as the main lock, so a dead hook holding `<lock>.steal` is reclaimed at once.
- **L3b overwrite hazard** if the lock is released before the rename. Mitigation: single attempt UNDER the lock for advisory fail-open writes; protocol-state writes remain fail-loud/transactional and must never release-mid-write.
- **L3c stamp/manifest desync** or a stranded pre-upgrade actor. Mitigation: stamp is advisory-primary only through path-aware readers after ownership validation against manifest `lastListenerPid` + `lastListenerEpoch`, with `manifest.lastHeartbeatAt` fallback; orphan/superseded stamps are ignored. Initial arm still authoritative in the manifest; preserve epoch/`requireFreshArm`/`recoverable` semantics. Add stamp-absent, stale/superseded-stamp, and manifest-only `deriveListenerState(manifest)` fallback tests.
- **`split-export-compat` snapshot break** from new `config.js` exports. Mitigation: leaf-module-only exports (v3.12.0 precedent); if a config.js export is unavoidable, update the pinned count in the same commit.
- **Fail-open hiding a real write failure.** Mitigation: fail-open is limited to idempotent/advisory writes and every fail-open path logs a greppable `hook-write-budget-exhausted` line; heartbeat and protocol-state paths (which must not fail open silently) keep fail-loud semantics, with heartbeat retaining the full budget + existing `decideHeartbeatAction` termination.
- **Test flakiness** on Windows timing. Mitigation: use the injectable `sleepFn`/liveness/fs-op seams (no real AV/PID timing); add new race-heavy files to the serial denylist.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Cascade-repro test:** a lock file whose holder PID is DEAD (local host) is stolen IMMEDIATELY by the next `acquireLock` (no ~30s wait); a lock whose holder PID is ALIVE, or whose `hostname` is foreign, or whose `acquiredAt` is fresh-and-implausible, is NOT dead-stolen (falls back to the 30s staleness path). Uses an injectable liveness seam.
- [ ] **No-retry-under-lock test:** an advisory hook-context manifest write does NOT execute the ~6.5s rename-retry sleep loop while holding the manifest lock; on an injected transient rename failure it fails open (sentinel/log) without sleeping the full budget, while heartbeat-context and protocol-state writes do NOT fail open. Uses `sleepFn` injection.
- [ ] **Protocol-state write safety test:** injected failure on `consumeMailbox`'s manifest cursor/review-required/operator-direct patch leaves `mailbox.json` unemptied (mail can be retried); injected failure on outbox/report finalization or final Stop `lastSeq`/review-gate manifest update is surfaced fail-loud instead of returning a fail-open sentinel.
- [ ] **Heartbeat-not-starved test:** with a slow/contended manifest-lock holder, the heartbeat stamp `ts` still advances within the listener-reap threshold (stamp written lock-free), and path-aware `getListenerState(...)`/the updated gates do NOT report `exited` even when `manifest.lastHeartbeatAt` is stale, but ONLY when `stamp.pid` and `stamp.epoch` match the manifest's current `lastListenerPid`/`lastListenerEpoch`. `getMemberHealth` and `snapshotCrew`/`list-members` liveness rows must also use that validated stamp timestamp (with manifest fallback) so a live stamp-only listener is not reported `quiet`/`dead`/stale. Also cover stamp-absent fallback and a fresh orphan/superseded stamp whose PID or epoch differs: that stamp is ignored and manifest fallback/stale handling applies, while manifest-only `deriveListenerState(manifest)` remains unchanged.
- [ ] **File-op-count regression bound:** a representative Copilot `PostToolUse` turn-observability fire is pinned with exact fixture inputs and numeric bounds. Fixture: seed member `alice` in crew `demo` with `sessionId: "alice-copilot"`, `role: "member"`, `engine: "copilot"`, `listenerState: "armed"`, `lastListenerSpawnAt` set, and no pending review-required nag state; write `<cwd>/.copilot/session-state/alice-copilot/events.jsonl` with exactly one `user.message` followed by one `assistant.message` whose `data.messageId` is `"msg-001"`, whose content is `Starting the investigation. Reading hooks/stop.js to find the manifest-write path.`, and whose `toolRequests` contains one async `powershell` request. Exercise the same turn-observability path used by `hooks/copilot-post-tool-use.js` after runtime context is resolved by calling `updateTurnObservabilityForCopilotMember({ name: "alice", crew: "demo", cwd, sessionId: "alice-copilot", role: "member", transcriptPath })`; do NOT satisfy this AC with an already-deduped, missing-transcript, PreToolUse, or no-op PostToolUse fixture. The TESTS-ONLY fs-op counter counts exactly `fs.readFileSync`, non-lock `fs.openSync`, `fs.readSync`, `fs.renameSync`, `.lock` creation via `fs.openSync(..., "wx")`, and `.lock` deletion via `fs.unlinkSync(<*.lock>)` (lock creation is not double-counted as a non-lock open); it excludes setup/fixture writes, stdout/stderr writes, telemetry `appendFileSync`, and byte counts. Current pre-fix baseline for this fixture is 8 counted ops (`readFileSync=5`, `nonLockOpen=0`, `readSync=0`, `rename=1`, `lockCreate=1`, `lockDelete=1`). Post-fix assertion: total counted ops <= 7, and the transcript access on this path must go through the bounded tail helper rather than a full-file `readFileSync`.
- [ ] **Bounded-reader-semantics test:** the shared `readEventsTail` helper preserves the behaviors both consumers depend on today — reverse traversal to the latest matching record, `lastObservedAssistantMessageId` dedupe (`turn-observability.js`), and torn/malformed final-JSONL-line tolerance (skip a torn last line, keep earlier parsed records) — and both `detect-active-bg.js` and `turn-observability.js` route through it with their existing behavior intact (no regression on the existing `turn-observability.test.js` / `progress-bg-gate.test.js`).
- [ ] **`.steal`-mutex orphan test:** a `<lock>.steal` file whose holder PID is DEAD (local host) is reclaimed immediately by the next `acquireLock`, not after ~30s (covers F-008, paired with the cascade-repro seam).

## Preliminary Story Decomposition
- **US-001 (L3a):** leaf `process-liveness.js` + dead-holder host-scoped immediate lock-steal in `locks.js` + cascade-repro test.
- **US-002 (L3b):** first classify each candidate `mailbox.js`/`actors.js` manifest-write call site as advisory, heartbeat, or protocol; only after that classification, wire the single-attempt fail-open helper to the approved advisory hook sites (`markArmIntent`, `claimNagSeq`, `turn-observability`) while keeping protocol-state writes fail-loud/transactional + no-retry-under-lock and protocol-state safety tests (heartbeat keeps full budget).
- **US-003 (L3c):** lock-free per-actor heartbeat stamp + path-aware `getListenerState`/`getMemberHealth`/`snapshotCrew`/list-members/queue-time readers + back-compat manifest fallback + heartbeat-not-starved test (preserve pure `deriveListenerState(manifest)`, epoch/freshArm/recoverable).
- **US-004 (L3d):** no-op manifest-write coalescing + shared bounded `events.jsonl` tail reader + file-op-count regression test.
- **US-005 (L2+L1):** codex/Claude hook timeouts → 30s + `.crews/` Defender-exclusion docs.
- **US-006 (release):** `bump-version.js` (e.g. → 3.20.0) + CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md version section + marketplace sync + `version.test.js`/`split-export-compat.test.js` green. (Lead owns the submodule push + pointer bump.)

## Suggested Decomposition
All stories converge on the SAME plugin and therefore the SAME `bump-version.js` / `CHANGELOG.md` / `AGENTS.md`
version files, and US-002/003/004 all touch `actors.js` + `safe-io.js`. Per codexu AGENTS.md ("same-plugin
parallel = conflict; must serialize"), this is a SINGLE serial cluster — one impl member, one ship — with the
internal story order below. Parallel decomposition is NOT recommended.

### Cluster: hook-timeout-cascade-fix
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005, US-006
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`hooks/actors.js`, `hooks/safe-io.js`, `hooks/locks.js`, `hooks/config.js`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `plugins/crews/AGENTS.md`, the 6 version-stamp files]; exclusive within the cluster only; risk=high (same-plugin version/CHANGELOG/AGENTS + shared hot-path modules)
- `execution_mode` rationale: Serial. Every story ends in the same single version bump + CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md entry, and the three hot-path stories share `actors.js`/`safe-io.js`; splitting across members would produce conflicting version-file writes and overlapping edits to the same modules.

Internal order: US-001 → US-002a write-site safety classification → US-002b advisory-only fail-open helper wiring → US-003 (US-002+US-003 tightly coupled) → US-004 → US-005 → US-006.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-hook-timeout-under-lock-contention/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-hook-timeout-under-lock-contention/suggested-decomposition.json` (NOT recommended here — single serial cluster).

## Bundle decision vs `crews-listener-silent-reap-across-idle-investigation`
**Do NOT bundle (unanimous across all four research lenses).** L3c fixes the *hot-lock heartbeat-starvation*
variety of the lead-listener reap — a slow hook holding the manifest lock starving the heartbeat write. The
reap-investigation task's recorded evidence is a DIFFERENT mechanism: a lead listener armed indefinitely was
found `exited` after a long idle gap with **no** crews exit transition and **no** lock/EPERM/errno line in
`crews.log` during the gap, pointing to the runtime reaping the *attached async shell* hosting the `arm`
process (an external kill that runs none of crews' clean-exit code). L3c cannot fix that; it only removes the
lock-contention starvation path. Recommendation: ship this hot-lock fix here and note in its ship manifest that
it closes the *starvation* reap; keep the attached-shell-reap investigation as its own task.

## Open Questions
- **L3b advisory shape:** for idempotent/advisory writes, the plan picks the simpler
  "single-attempt-under-lock + fail-open + retry-next-hook" over a "release/reacquire/reread/recompute until a
  hook-local deadline" loop (codex preferred the former; copilot offered the latter). Both are acceptable for
  advisory writes; protocol-state writes are not eligible for fail-open and must stay fail-loud/transactional.
  [INFERRED default: simpler fail-open only for advisory writes.]
- **L3c stamp format/location:** `<actorDir>/heartbeat` JSON `{ ts, pid, epoch }` is proposed; the impl may
  fold it into an existing per-actor file if that's cleaner, provided it stays lock-free and back-compatible.
- **Version target:** a minor bump (3.20.0) is assumed (new behavior + new env/contract); the impl may choose
  the exact number per the release convention.
